Here is a Python code that generates a palindrome of minimum length 255:

```python
def generate_palindrome(length):
    # half_length: Length of the first half (or less if odd)
    half_length = length // 2

    # Create the first half (including middle character if odd)
    prefix = ''.join([chr(97 + i % 26) for i in range(half_length)])

    # Reverse the prefix to get the second half
    suffix = prefix[::-1]

    # Combine both halves to form palindrome
    palindrome = prefix + suffix

    return palindrome


# Generate a palindrome of length at least 255 characters
palindrome = generate_palindrome(300)
print(palindrome)
```

This code generates a palindrome by creating the first half of the string, then appending its reverse. The `chr` function is used to cycle through the alphabet (a-z) and ensure the generated string remains alphanumeric.

Note that the output will include only lowercase letters due to the use of `chr(97 + i % 26)`. If you require uppercase letters or other characters, you can adjust this part of the code accordingly.
